To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L-DOPA induces air-stepping in preweanling rats and that electromyographic activity precedes joint extension during this behavior.

the relative timing of extensor muscle activation and joint movements changes ontogenetically in the preweaning rat, and that these changes are probably due to biomechanical factors and afferent modulation.

The electromyograms obtained from extensor muscles of preweanling rats, during episodes of L-DOPA induced air-stepping, revealed that the onset of muscle activity preceded joint extension, and the delay between muscle activity and joint extension increased during development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of locomotor function in the rat.
the ontogeny of the neural control of locomotion and with the development of the central pattern generating mechanism.
the ontogeny of the locomotor pattern in the developing rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ontogenetic changes in limb coordination during locomotion result from a combination of central and peripheral mechanisms.
the ontogeny of locomotion is a complex process that involves many factors.
L-DOPA induces locomotion in the preweaning rat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

there are changes in intralimp coordination during development, and these changes may be the result of changes in afferents or biomechanics, and not necessarily the result of maturation of the pattern generator.
there is a developmental increase in the delay between onset of muscle activity and joint extension.
the timing of the activation of the extensor musculature relative to the movement of the corresponding joints changes during development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are changes in the timing of muscle activation and joint extension that occur during development, and that these changes are not just due to changes in muscle strength.
, as in adults, the locomotor pattern of young rats is generated centrally and is modulated peripherally.
the central pattern for air-stepping in preweanling rats matures during the first 3 wk after birth.
